topic: Stung by a jellyfish: pee on it or hot water?
title: Stung By A Jellyfish
idea: The famous pee trick makes stinging cells fire; sea water, careful removal and hot water are what help.
hook: A jellyfish just stung you. Pee on it, or hot water?

beats.line: Tentacle bits stick to your skin, with stingers still loaded.
beats.see: Close up on a leg: glowing tentacle strands cling to it, zoom into tiny cocked harpoon cells. Zoom on 'stingers', cells glow on 'loaded'.

beats.line: In lab tests, pee made those cells fire.
beats.see: Lab dish with a tentacle; a yellow drop falls in and dozens of tiny harpoons fire at once. Drop on 'pee', harpoons on 'fire'. Card A gets a red X.
A tap drips onto the dish and a second volley of harpoons fires. Volley on 'same'.

beats.line: Hot water is the answer. It eases the pain better than ice.
beats.see: Card B HOT WATER gets a green check; split screen pain meter, ice side barely drops, hot water side drops low. Check on 'Hot', meters on 'better'.

beats.line: One. Rinse with sea water, not fresh.
beats.see: Step card 1 SEA WATER; a cup scoops seawater and pours it over the leg; a tap icon gets crossed out. Pour on 'Rinse', X on 'fresh'.

beats.line: Two. Lift the tentacles off, but never with bare fingers.
beats.see: Step card 2 LIFT OFF; a gloved hand peels the strands away, a bare hand icon is crossed out. Peel on 'Lift', X on 'bare'.

beats.line: Three. Hot water, about one hundred thirteen degrees, for about twenty minutes.
beats.see: Step card 3 HOT WATER; leg in a steaming tub, thermometer at 113 F, a twenty minute timer runs. Thermometer on 'thirteen', timer on 'twenty'.

beats.line: In the tropics, call for help. A box jellyfish can kill in minutes.
beats.see: Background turns tropical; a box shaped jellyfish drifts in, phone dials an emergency number with a red warning frame. Phone on 'call', red frame on 'kill'.

end.line: Pee stays in the toilet. Hot water goes on the sting.
end.see: Card A flips onto a toilet icon, card B slides onto the leg with steam rising. Toilet on 'toilet', steam on 'sting', loops into the hook sting.

description: Stung by a jellyfish: pee on it or hot water? The famous trick makes the stingers fire.

facts.claim: Urine does not help; in lab tests on Portuguese man o' war it made stinging cells fire. Fresh water did too.
Hot water, about 45 C (113 F) for about 20 minutes, relieves pain better than ice.
facts.source: Wilcox & Yanagihara, Toxins 2016 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4848624 ; Cochrane review CD009688; Healthdirect https://www.healthdirect.gov.au/jellyfish-stings

facts.claim: Rinse with sea water, not fresh water; remove tentacles, not with bare fingers.
A box jellyfish sting can kill within minutes; call emergency services for tropical stings.

notes: Correct card: B HOT WATER. Card A shortened to 'PEE' (the spoken line still says 'pee on it') because cards are max two words. 113 degrees is the Fahrenheit conversion of the allowed 45 C for a US audience, not a sharper number; on screen show 113 F. The lab test was on Portuguese man o' war; the script says 'in lab tests' and does not claim it holds for every species. Vinegar is deliberately not mentioned (species dependent, see FACTS). 'Stingers still loaded' is a plain description of unfired stinging cells. Risk: viewers should not scald themselves; keep the thermometer at 113 F, do not add 'as hot as you can stand'. Stake number sits in step three (one hundred thirteen degrees, twenty minutes); the FACTS file has no stronger on-screen number for this topic.
